title: Mixed-Slope Roof Replacement in Fallbrook
summary: A Fallbrook replacement combining Owens Corning Duration COOL shingles with a Johns Manville two-layer modified-bitumen system at the low-slope areas.
conditions: The home combined pitched roof areas, low-slope sections, a dead valley, plank decking, and existing solar stanchions, so one roofing material could not responsibly address every condition.
scope: Overlaid the existing plank deck with CDX plywood to create a suitable substrate.
Installed Owens Corning Duration COOL Mountainside shingles on the pitched roof areas.
Installed a Johns Manville two-layer torch-applied modified-bitumen system at the garage, low-slope areas, and dead valley.
Waterproofed the existing solar stanchions as part of the new assembly.
materials: Owens Corning Duration COOL Mountainside shingles
Johns Manville two-layer torch-applied modified bitumen
lesson: Mixed-slope homes often need more than one roof system. The pitch, drainage, deck, penetrations, and transitions should determine the material used in each area.

title: Owens Corning Duration Cool Roof Replacement in Fallbrook
summary: A documented Fallbrook roof replacement finished with Owens Corning Duration Cool shingles in Night Sky.
conditions: The existing roof had reached the point where a complete replacement was the dependable path forward.
scope: Removed the existing roofing system and prepared the deck for the new assembly.
Installed a complete Owens Corning shingle roofing system.
Finished the roof with Duration Cool shingles in the Night Sky color.
lesson: A cool-roof shingle can satisfy California performance requirements without forcing a homeowner into a light or washed-out roof color.

title: Steep-Slope Concrete Tile Roof Repair in Escondido
summary: A targeted Escondido repair where the steep pitch required secure tile support and focused waterproofing around the chimney.
conditions: The repair area was on a steep concrete-tile roof and included a chimney transition that needed additional self-adhered protection.
scope: Carefully removed and staged the existing concrete tile in the repair area.
Installed 30-pound asphalt felt and wood tile battens.
Installed Titanium PSU30 self-adhered underlayment around the chimney.
Reset the existing concrete roof tile over the repaired assembly.
materials: Existing concrete roof tile, removed and reset
lesson: On a steep tile roof, secure batten support and careful chimney waterproofing are essential parts of a durable localized repair.

title: Westlake Saxony 900 Tile Roof in Rancho Santa Fe
summary: A finished Rancho Santa Fe tile roofing project using Westlake Saxony 900 concrete tile.
conditions: The project called for a durable tile assembly that fit the scale and architectural character of the home.
scope: Prepared the roof for the new tile assembly.
Installed the tile system with careful layout at ridges, hips, eaves, and transitions.
Completed the roof with Westlake Saxony 900 concrete tile.
lesson: On a detailed home, the layout and finishing work around hips, ridges, walls, and transitions matter as much as the field tile.

title: Owens Corning Duration Cool Sand Castle Roof in Poway
summary: A Poway shingle roof replacement completed with Owens Corning Duration Cool shingles in Sand Castle.
conditions: The home needed a complete roofing upgrade with a finished color that complemented the property.
scope: Removed the old roof and evaluated the exposed deck.
Installed the new roofing components as a coordinated system.
Finished with Owens Corning Duration Cool shingles in Sand Castle.
lesson: The roof color should be selected as part of the whole exterior, not from a small sample viewed by itself.

title: Tile Lift & Lay Underlayment Renewal in Temecula
summary: A Temecula tile lift-and-lay project that preserved the existing roof tile while renewing the waterproofing beneath it.
conditions: The visible tile remained useful, but the aging waterproofing layer beneath the tile required attention.
scope: Carefully removed and staged the existing roof tile.
Renewed the underlayment and critical waterproofing details.
Reset the existing tile to preserve the original appearance.
materials: Existing roof tile, removed and reset
New tile-roof underlayment and flashing components
lesson: Tile is the weathering surface. The underlayment below it is the primary waterproofing layer, so a roof can look good from the street while still needing renewal underneath.

title: Shingle Roof Replacement and Obsolete Solar Equipment Removal in Escondido
summary: An Escondido replacement where obsolete rooftop solar water-heating equipment was removed and concealed wood damage was corrected before the new roof was installed.
conditions: After tear-off and equipment removal, dry rot and damaged plywood sheathing were visible and could be repaired correctly.
scope: Removed the old shingle roof and obsolete rooftop solar water-heating equipment.
Repaired dry rot and replaced damaged plywood sheathing found during tear-off.
Installed a complete replacement shingle roof over the corrected deck.
lesson: Tear-off exposes the actual deck. A dependable replacement includes correcting damaged wood before it is covered by the new roof.

title: Commercial DIBITEN Flat Roof Replacement in Escondido
summary: A commercial Escondido project that replaced an aging tar-and-gravel roof with a two-ply Johns Manville DIBITEN APP system.
conditions: The existing tar-and-gravel roof and rooftop equipment layout required coordinated removal, curb work, drainage work, and waterproofing.
scope: Removed the existing tar-and-gravel roof.
Temporarily removed four rooftop equipment units and installed new equipment curbs.
Replaced four roof drains.
Installed a two-ply Johns Manville DIBITEN APP torch-down system.
Completed adjoining tile repairs at the mixed-roof transitions.
materials: Johns Manville DIBITEN APP modified bitumen
lesson: Commercial flat-roof performance depends on the complete drainage and penetration plan, not only the membrane covering the open field.

title: White Granulated Torch-Down Roof Replacement in Point Loma
summary: A Point Loma modified-bitumen replacement for a homeowner who wanted a bright white roof after two earlier single-layer roofs leaked.
conditions: Two prior single-layer torch-down roofs had leaked. After reviewing a TPO option, the homeowner chose a bright white granulated cap sheet.
scope: Removed the failed roofing layers and prepared the low-slope roof.
Detailed the chimney, skylight, penetrations, transitions, and perimeter.
Installed a traditional three-layer Johns Manville DIBITEN APP system with a fiberglass base sheet, smooth APP membrane, and bright white granulated cap sheet.
materials: Johns Manville DIBITEN smooth APP membrane
Johns Manville bright white granulated cap sheet
lesson: The number of plies and the quality of perimeter and penetration details matter. A roof should be evaluated as a full assembly rather than by its visible cap sheet alone.

service: Shingle Roof and Structural Wood Repair
title: Shingle Roof Replacement and Extensive Wood Repair in City Heights
summary: A City Heights tear-off that included extensive rafter-tail, shiplap, and fascia replacement before the new cool-roof shingles were installed.
conditions: Tear-off exposed deteriorated roof-edge framing and sheathing that required repair before the home could receive a dependable new roof.
scope: Completed a full tear-off.
Replaced approximately 18 rotted rafter tails.
Replaced more than 100 feet of deteriorated shiplap and fascia.
Installed synthetic underlayment and self-adhered ice-and-water protection.
Finished with Owens Corning Duration Cool shingles in Shasta White.
lesson: Edge rot is not cosmetic. Rafter tails, shiplap, fascia, drip edge, and the roof covering must work together to create a durable roof edge.

title: LifeTile Lift & Lay with Titanium Underlayment in Oceanside
summary: An Oceanside tile lift-and-lay that reset the existing LifeTile over a new two-layer Titanium underlayment assembly.
conditions: The existing LifeTile could be preserved, while the deck, wood details, valleys, and aged waterproofing below required renewal.
scope: Removed and staged the existing LifeTile.
Completed deck and wood repairs where needed.
Installed two layers of Titanium UDL50 underlayment.
Installed Titanium PSU30 at valleys.
Reset the existing tile over the renewed waterproofing assembly.
lesson: A lift-and-lay can leave the roof looking familiar from the street while substantially renewing the waterproofing system below.

title: Uniflex Silicone Roof Restoration in La Jolla
summary: A La Jolla low-slope roof restoration using a Uniflex silicone coating system.
conditions: The existing low-slope roof was evaluated as a restoration candidate rather than automatically being sent to full replacement.
scope: Prepared and cleaned the existing roof surface.
Addressed seams, penetrations, and transitions before coating.
Applied the Uniflex silicone restoration system to create a reflective finished surface.
lesson: A coating is not paint. Successful restoration begins with substrate qualification, preparation, and reinforced detailing before the field coating is applied.
